# libresprite_ca_generator

A LibreSprite script that paints a real cellular-automaton cave pattern —
generated by this project's existing `fung_ai_v2.py` engine (`generate`,
rule `B3/S23`) — into the active sprite's cel: wall cells get a dark-stone
color, floor cells get a tan color.

This package contains exactly one file: `libresprite_ca_generator.js`. That
one file *is* the extension — see "Why no manifest / no zip" below for why
there's nothing else to install.

## What it does

Paints a fixed 40x30 cave grid (rule `B3/S23`, 12 ticks, seed 2026,
coverage ≈0.185, `playable=true`) into the active cel using
`app.pixelColor.rgba(60,56,54,255)` for walls and `rgba(214,188,140,255)`
for floor. The grid data is embedded directly in the script as a literal
array — see "Known constraints" below for why.

## Install

LibreSprite has **no Aseprite-style `.aseprite-extension`/`package.json`
manifest system**. Its real extension mechanism (confirmed by testing
against a real v1.2-dev Windows build, not assumed from docs — see this
project's `research/aseprite_notes.md`) is a flat scripts folder plus a
"Rescan Scripts" command:

1. In LibreSprite, run **File > Scripts > Open Scripts Folder**
   (or `app.command.OpenScriptsFolder()` from the console). On Windows this
   is `%APPDATA%\LibreSprite\scripts`.
2. Copy `libresprite_ca_generator.js` from this folder into that scripts
   folder.
3. Run **File > Scripts > Rescan Scripts**
   (or `app.command.RescanScripts()`). The filename (minus `.js`) now
   appears as a runnable entry under **File > Scripts**.

## Invoke

- **Interactive (normal use):** open or create a sprite, then run
  **File > Scripts > libresprite_ca_generator**. This is the "Generate CA
  Pattern" command — it resizes the active sprite to 40x30 if needed and
  paints the pattern into layer 0 / cel 0 of the active sprite
  (`app.activeSprite`).
- **Batch/CLI (used for all verification of this package):**
  ```
  libresprite.exe -b --script "<path-to-installed-script>\libresprite_ca_generator.js"
  ```
  In this mode there is no "active sprite" (`app.activeSprite` is
  `undefined` in `-b` batch mode even with a file loaded — a real, tested
  constraint, not an assumption), so the script falls back to opening a
  blank canvas (`extensions/ca_generator_blank.png` in the source repo,
  referenced by absolute path in the script) and saves the result to
  `godot_project/imported_assets/ca_generated/ca_pattern.ase`.

## Known constraints / limitations (discovered by direct testing)

- **No subprocess capability.** LibreSprite's JS engine exposes only three
  top-level globals (`app`, `storage`, `ColorMode`) with no exec/spawn/
  subprocess object anywhere in the surface. The script cannot shell out to
  `python fung_ai_v2.py generate` at runtime.
- **CA data is pre-generated and embedded, not live-generated.** Because of
  the constraint above, and because `storage.fetch()` on local `file://`
  paths was tested directly and found non-functional (never resolves, even
  after 300 x 20ms poll cycles), the script embeds the literal,
  unmodified output of one real CLI run of `fung_ai_v2.py generate
  --rule B3/S23 --width 40 --height 30 --ticks 12 --seed 2026` as a JS
  array. Every install of this script paints the same fixed pattern; it
  does not generate a new one per run.
- **The interactive click-path (Scripts menu on a GUI-open sprite) was not
  manually click-tested.** This package was verified end-to-end via the
  batch/CLI path above, which exercises the identical
  `image.putPixel`/`sprite.saveAs` code the interactive path uses, and
  `app.activeSprite` is consulted first exactly per the documented/tested
  API shape — but no human click-through in the real GUI has been done.
- `app.command.NewFile()` and other UI-driving commands segfault in batch
  mode — irrelevant to this script (it never calls them) but worth knowing
  if you extend it.
- `SCRIPTING.md` (LibreSprite's official docs) is stale in several places
  versus the real v1.2-dev build (e.g. `command`/`pixelColor` are
  documented as top-level globals but actually live at `app.command`/
  `app.pixelColor`). See `research/aseprite_notes.md` in the source repo
  for the full list of discrepancies found by live enumeration.

## Packaging verification (this pass)

This exact copy of the script was tested from a packaged location, not
just its original `extensions/` location:

1. Copied `libresprite_ca_generator.js` from this `dist/` folder into the
   real Windows scripts folder, `%APPDATA%\LibreSprite\scripts`.
2. Ran it from that location headlessly:
   `libresprite.exe -b --script "%APPDATA%\LibreSprite\scripts\libresprite_ca_generator.js"`.
   Output: `painted 40x30 cells (rule=B3/S23, ticks=12, seed=2026,
   coverage=0.1850000023841858, playable=true)` — identical to the
   original verification run from `extensions/`.
3. Exported the resulting `.ase` back to a PNG via LibreSprite's own CLI
   and pixel-diffed it against a fresh, independent run of
   `fung_ai_v2.py generate` with the same parameters: **1200/1200 cells
   matched, 0 mismatches.**

This confirms the package works correctly when installed exactly as this
README describes, not only when run from the source repo layout.
